Quadratic Forms and Covariance Matrices

The variance of a book of N assets is a quadratic form in its weights: how the sample covariance matrix is built, why the variance it gives is never negative, and how software can still make it so.

Volume II · Linear Algebra for PortfoliosBuilds on LM3 · LM7 · LM8 · LM9Leads to LM11 · LM12 · LM16 · LM19 · LM20 · LM27 · LM28 · LM29 · LM30 · LM31 · LM43Time ≈ 3 h + labPDF A4 print edition
Learning Outcomes
MasteryAfter this module you should be able to:
1evaluate a quadratic form x⊤Mx as a double sum, and explain why only the symmetric part of M matters
2build the sample covariance matrix Σ^=X~⊤X~/T from a matrix of returns, annualize it, and convert it to a correlation matrix and back
3compute the variance of a daily-rebalanced portfolio as w⊤Σ^w, and split it into variance and covariance terms
4test a symmetric matrix for positive definiteness and semidefiniteness with leading principal minors, pivots and all principal minors
5explain why a sample covariance matrix is positive semidefinite, when it is singular, and how pairwise deletion produces a matrix that is not
6derive the gradient and Hessian of a⊤w and w⊤Mw, and price a change of weights exactly with the expansion of a quadratic form
7prove that a quadratic function is convex exactly when its matrix is positive semidefinite
8compute covariance matrices, portfolio variances and definiteness tests in NumPy and Polars with the right orientation, divisor and tolerance
Learning Module Overview
  • A quadratic form x⊤Mx=∑i​∑j​mij​xi​xj​ depends only on the symmetric part of M. Its sign, not the sign of any entry, decides whether a matrix can be a covariance matrix.
  • The sample covariance matrix Σ^=X~⊤X~/T of U28, the 28 leaf sector indices that FinMind serves daily, has 406 distinct entries. Annualizing multiplies it by A=245.48; dividing each entry by two standard deviations converts it to the correlation matrix.
  • The sample variance of a daily-rebalanced book is exactly w⊤Σ^w. An equal-weight book of the 28 sectors had 15.75% volatility from 2008 to 2026, below every sector but one, and covariances made 92.8% of its variance.
  • A sample covariance matrix is positive semidefinite, because w⊤Σ^w=∥X~w∥2/T, and positive definite exactly when the centred returns have full column rank.
  • A symmetric matrix is positive definite exactly when its leading principal minors, or its pivots, are all positive. Positive semidefiniteness needs every principal minor, as diag(0,−1) shows.
  • With T≤N returns the sample covariance matrix is singular: the 28 sectors on their latest 28 returns give rank 27. Pairwise deletion can do worse: adding 0050, 00631L and 00679B on their own dates gives a pairwise covariance matrix that is not positive semidefinite.
  • The gradient of w⊤Mw is 2Mw for symmetric M, and the second-order expansion of a quadratic form is exact: moving 1/28 of the book from GlassCeramic to CommunicationsInternet would have cut its 2008–2026 sample volatility from 15.75% to 15.28%.
  • A quadratic function is convex exactly when its matrix is positive semidefinite, and strictly convex exactly when it is positive definite.

1Introduction

LM7 measured the risk of two assets with two variances and a covariance. A book of N assets needs N variances and N(N−1)/2 covariances, kept in a matrix. Its variance is a quadratic form in the weights. This module builds the sample covariance matrix from returns. It shows why the variance it gives is never negative, and how a risk system can still print a negative one.

Motivating CaseTwenty-eight volatilities, one number

A desk holds U28, the 28 leaf sector indices that FinMind serves daily, in equal weights and rebalances the book every day. Over 4,382 daily returns, from 2 December 2008 to 8 October 2026, the sectors' annualized volatilities run from 13.67% (CommunicationsInternet) to 35.31% (GlassCeramic). They average 21.94% (Exhibit 1).

The book's volatility was 15.75%, below every sector but one and below TAIEX's 17.82%. The 28 variance terms alone would give a volatility of only 4.22%. Which numbers account for the rest of the book's variance? A 28×28 covariance matrix holds 406 distinct entries. Why can the answer never fall below zero, and how can a risk system still print a negative variance?

Sections 2 and 3 define quadratic forms and the sample covariance matrix, and Sections 4 to 6 answer the case's three questions. Section 7 differentiates quadratic forms, and Section 8 does the same computations in Python.

NoteNotation for this module

U28 is the set of the 28 leaf sector indices among the 30 TWSE sector indices that FinMind serves daily: all except the aggregates Electronic and ChemicalBiotechnologyMedicalCare. TWSE's four sector indices with base date 30 June 2023 have no daily series there. S3 is Semiconductor, FinancialInsurance and Food; S5 adds Plastics and ShippingTransportation.

M, K: generic matrices, entries mij​; Msym​:=21​(M+M⊤); h(x):=x⊤Mx; x, y: generic vectors (in Example 9 and the widget, positions in standard-deviation units); Mk​: the leading k×k block, detMk​ its leading principal minor and dk​:=detMk​/detMk−1​ the pivot of step k (as in LM9), with detM0​:=1; adjM: the adjugate.

X: the T×N returns, with entry xtj​=Rj,t​, the return of asset j on date t; Rˉ: sample means; X~: centred returns, entries x~tj​; Σ^: the sample covariance matrix, entries σ^ij​ and σ^ii​=si2​; s: standard deviations; C: the correlation matrix; Σ^3​, C3​: the S3 blocks of Σ^ and C (named for S3; they are not leading blocks); Σ^pw​, Cpw​: the matrices that pairwise deletion builds, which come from no single sample; var, cov: averages of the N diagonal and N(N−1) off-diagonal entries of Σ^; Tij​: the number of dates on which assets i and j both have returns.

w: weights summing to 1, rebalanced daily; sp2​:=w⊤Σ^w; f: exposures, which need not sum to 1 (Exhibit 10, Practice Problem 8); a: coefficients; Δ: a change of weights or exposures; ω∈[0,1]: a mixing weight (the usual λ and t already mean a multiplier and a date); H: a Hessian; u: the function of Practice Problem 8. Counts: N assets (i, j), T returns (t), never a horizon; k is a block size or an elimination step. Moments divide by T (LM3), and A=245.48 comes from the U28 sample.

NoteResearch hygiene

Every matrix in this module describes 2008–2026. It is not a forecast, and no result here is tested on later data (LM11 compares periods; LM30 treats estimation error). Every result is descriptive. Example 9 describes a constructed sample: its returns are real, but the author chose which years to drop.

2Quadratic Forms and Symmetric Matrices

evaluate a quadratic form x⊤Mx as a double sum, and explain why only the symmetric part of M matters

Section 3 builds a covariance matrix from daily returns with (10.2). For S3, on the 4,382 returns of the case and annualized, the matrix is, in squared percentage points (%²),

AΣ^3​=​570.34261.83162.26​261.83363.73191.35​162.26191.35283.54​​.

Put a vector of positions on both sides of AΣ^3​. For e1​=(1,0,0)⊤, all in Semiconductor, e1⊤​(AΣ^3​)e1​ selects the entry 570.34, a volatility of 570.34​=23.88%. For (1,−1,0)⊤, long Semiconductor and short FinancialInsurance, it gives 570.34+363.73−2(261.83)=410.41, or 20.26%. For the mix (0.5,0.3,0.2)⊤ it gives 320.6, or 17.91%. Each result is the variance of a daily-rebalanced book, as Section 4 proves.

DefinitionQuadratic form

Let M be an N×N matrix. The quadratic form of M is the function

h(x)=x⊤Mx=i=1∑N​j=1∑N​mij​xi​xj​,
for x∈RN.

The double sum meets mij​ and mji​ with the same product xi​xj​, so only their sum matters:

x⊤Mx=x⊤Msym​x,Msym​:=21​(M+M⊤).​(10.1)

In matrix language, x⊤Mx is a number, so it equals its own transpose x⊤M⊤x, and (10.1) averages the two. From here on, a quadratic form has a symmetric matrix unless a sentence says otherwise. The form recovers its entries: h(ei​)=mii​, and h(ei​+ej​)=mii​+mjj​+2mij​ then gives mij​.

The level curve h(x)=1 of a form in two variables shows its type (Exhibit 2). A form that is positive away from 0 gives an ellipse. A form that is never negative but vanishes along a line gives two parallel lines, and a form that takes both signs gives a hyperbola. The test (7.4) of LM7 is the case N=2: completing the square shows that m11​>0 and detM>0 make the form positive.

Example 1The cross term decides

Let

M=(10​41​).
The matrix M has positive diagonal entries and detM=1>0, so a careless reading of (7.4) calls the form positive. Evaluate h at (1,−1)⊤, and test Msym​.

Solution

The form is h(x)=x12​+4x1​x2​+x22​, so h(1,−1)=1−4+1=−2<0. The symmetric part is

Msym​=(12​21​),detMsym​=1−4=−3<0,​
and by (7.4) the form takes both signs. The test reads a symmetric matrix; the determinant of M itself says nothing about h.

Knowledge Check 1

Write h(x)=3x12​−4x1​x2​+x22​ as x⊤Mx with a symmetric M, and decide its type.

Answer

The diagonal is m11​=3 and m22​=1, and m12​=m21​=−2, half the coefficient of x1​x2​. Then detM=3−4=−1<0, so the form takes both signs: h(1,0)=3 but h(1,2)=3−8+4=−1.

3The Sample Covariance Matrix

build the sample covariance matrix Σ^=X~⊤X~/T from a matrix of returns, annualize it, and convert it to a correlation matrix and back
Example 2A covariance matrix by hand

Semiconductor and FinancialInsurance fell together after the 2025 Qingming holiday. The table gives their daily returns R1,t​ and R2,t​ on 7, 8 and 9 April 2025 and the deviations x~tj​=Rj,t​−Rˉj​ from the mean. The first return runs from the close of 2 April. Compute the sample covariance matrix, with divisor T=3, and the correlation.

Date R1,t​ (%) R2,t​ (%) x~t1​ x~t2​
7 Apr −9.95 −9.89 −3.8133 −4.90
8 Apr −3.99 +0.53 2.1467 5.52
9 Apr −4.47 −5.61 1.6667 −0.62
Mean −6.1367 −4.99 0 0
Solution

Each entry of Σ^ averages products of deviations over the three dates, in %²:

Date x~t12​ x~t1​x~t2​ x~t22​
7 Apr 14.5413 18.6852 24.0100
8 Apr 4.6083 11.8498 30.4704
9 Apr 2.7779 −1.0334 0.3844
Mean: σ^11​, σ^12​, σ^22​ 7.3092 9.8339 18.2883

So the correlation is

ρ=7.3092×18.2883​9.8339​=0.851.
Three days of a sell-off give 0.851; the 4,382 returns of the sample give 0.575 (Example 3).

Stack the T daily return vectors as the rows of a T×N matrix X. Row t is Rt⊤​, and column j holds asset j's returns (LM8). The sample means form the vector Rˉ=X⊤1/T, and subtracting it from every row centres the data: X~=X−1Rˉ⊤. Example 2 averaged products of centred columns. In matrix form,

Σ^=T1​X~⊤X~=T1​t=1∑T​(Rt​−Rˉ)(Rt​−Rˉ)⊤.(10.2)

The first form takes dot products of columns: entry (i,j) is centred column i dotted with centred column j, divided by T. The second form adds T matrices, one for each date. Both give the same entries,

σ^ij​=T1​t=1∑T​(Ri,t​−Rˉi​)(Rj,t​−Rˉj​),

so the matrix is symmetric, and its diagonal holds the variances si2​. Exhibit 3 follows the shapes for U28. The matrix Σ^ summarizes the sample; the covariance matrix of a random vector, which it estimates, is defined in LM16.

Dividing entry (i,j) by si​sj​ gives the correlation matrix, and multiplying reverses the step:

C=diag(s)−1Σ^diag(s)−1,Σ^=diag(s)Cdiag(s).​(10.3)

A diagonal matrix on the left scales the rows, and on the right it scales the columns. Entry (i,j) of C is also the cosine of the angle between centred columns i and j (LM8, (8.9)). Annualizing multiplies every entry of Σ^ by A and every si​ by A​, so it leaves C unchanged. Exhibit 4 shows C for U28.

Example 3From the covariance matrix to the correlation matrix

Find the volatilities and the correlation matrix of S3 from AΣ^3​ of Section 2.

Solution

The volatilities are the square roots of the diagonal: 570.34​=23.88%, 363.73​=19.07% and 283.54​=16.84%. Dividing each off-diagonal entry by its two volatilities, for example 261.83/(23.88×19.07)=0.575, gives

C3​=​10.5750.403​0.57510.596​0.4030.5961​​.
The way back multiplies: 23.88×19.07×0.575=261.85, close to 261.83 but not equal, because each factor was rounded. Practice Problem 4 rebuilds the whole matrix this way.

PitfallDivisor and orientation in software

np.cov treats each row as a variable and, by default, divides by the number of observations minus 1. On a T×N array of returns, pass rowvar=False, ddof=0: with rowvar=False alone the divisor is T−1. Dividing by T−1 removes a small bias under assumptions that LM20 states. With T=4,382 it multiplies a volatility by T/(T−1)​=1.000114: a relative change of 0.0114%, not 0.0114 percentage points.

導讀二次形式與樣本共變異數矩陣

二次形式（quadratic form）x⊤Mx 就是把每一格 mij​ 乘上 xi​xj​ 再全部加總，所以只有對稱部分（symmetric part）有作用，判斷正負時一定要先把矩陣對稱化。樣本共變異數矩陣（sample covariance matrix）Σ^ 的第 (i,j) 格，是中心化（centring）後第 i 行與第 j 行的內積（dot product）再除以 T，對角線是變異數（variance），其餘是共變異數（covariance）。28 個類股指數一共有 406 個不同的數字。每格除以兩個標準差（standard deviation）就得到相關矩陣（correlation matrix），乘回去又回到共變異數矩陣；年化只改變單位，不改變相關係數（correlation coefficient）。

Knowledge Check 2

A return matrix has T=250 rows and N=5 columns. Give the shapes of Rˉ, X~, Σ^ and X~X~⊤. Which one is the covariance matrix, and how many distinct entries does it have?

Answer

The mean vector Rˉ is 5×1, the centred matrix X~ is 250×5, and Σ^=X~⊤X~/T is 5×5, with 5+10=15 distinct entries. The product X~X~⊤ is 250×250: it compares dates, not assets, and it is not a covariance matrix.

4Portfolio Variance as a Quadratic Form

compute the variance of a daily-rebalanced portfolio as w⊤Σ^w, and split it into variance and covariance terms

Hold weights w that sum to 1, and rebalance to them every day. The book's daily returns are then the vector Xw (LM8, (8.12)), with mean Rˉ⊤w, so centring gives X~w. Its variance with divisor T is

sp2​​=T1​(X~w)⊤(X~w)=w⊤(T1​X~⊤X~)w=w⊤Σ^w.​(10.4)

The identity is exact: the sample variance of the rebalanced book equals the quadratic form of Σ^ at w. It needs constant weights. A buy-and-hold book's weights drift with prices (LM9), so its returns are not Xw for one w. The first expression in (10.4) is a squared length divided by T, so

w⊤Σ^w=T∥X~w∥2​≥0.(10.5)

In full, (10.4) is the double sum ∑i​∑j​wi​wj​σ^ij​, with N variance terms wi2​si2​ on the diagonal and N(N−1) covariance terms off it. For two assets it is the variance of LM7, w12​σ^11​+2w1​w2​σ^12​+w22​σ^22​.

Example 4A three-sector mix

Find the annualized volatility of the S3 mix w=(0.5,0.3,0.2)⊤, rebalanced daily, and compare it with the weighted average of the three volatilities.

Solution

Exhibit 5 lists the nine terms Awi​wj​σ^ij​, which sum to 320.62 (%²), so the volatility is 320.62​=17.91%. The weighted average of the volatilities is 0.5(23.88)+0.3(19.07)+0.2(16.84)=21.03%. The mix is 3.12 percentage points less volatile, because every correlation is below 1.

The gap is general. For non-negative weights, the triangle inequality (8.8) gives sp​≤w⊤s, which LM8 states as (8.11): a long-only book is never more volatile than the weighted average of its parts.

With equal weights wi​=1/N, the double sum splits into the N diagonal entries and the N(N−1) others:

sp2​=N21​i∑​j∑​σ^ij​=Nvar​+(1−N1​)cov.(10.6)

As N grows, the first term shrinks like 1/N, while the second approaches cov.

Example 5Equal weights on 28 sectors

In the case, the 28 daily variances average var=2.0328×10−4, and the 756 off-diagonal entries average cov=9.7254×10−5. Find the book's volatility and the share of its variance that comes from covariances. Then find the limit of (10.6) as N grows with both averages held fixed.

Solution

By (10.6), the daily variance is

sp2​​=282.0328×10−4​+2827​×9.7254×10−5=7.260×10−6+9.378×10−5=1.0104×10−4.​
Annualized, Asp2​=0.024803, and the volatility is 0.024803​=15.75%.

The covariance term is 9.378/10.104=92.8% of the variance, and the variance terms are the other 7.2%. On their own they would give a volatility of A×7.260×10−6​=4.22%, the case's 4.22%. Volatilities do not add, so 4.22% is not a part of 15.75%; the split holds for the variance only.

With both averages fixed, sp2​ tends to cov, so the volatility tends to Acov​=15.45%. This limit is a thought experiment: each sector added to a real book brings its own variance and covariances.

PitfallA split of the form, not of the assets

The diagonal and off-diagonal terms split the quadratic form, not the risk of each asset. Splitting sp2​ into one share per asset, and judging which split is meaningful, is the subject of LM27 and LM31. This module stops at the gradient (Section 7).

導讀投資組合變異數就是二次形式

每天再平衡到固定權重 w 的投資組合，日報酬就是 Xw，它的樣本變異數（sample variance）正好等於 w⊤Σ^w，沒有任何近似。展開後有 N 個變異數項與 N(N−1) 個共變異數（covariance）項：28 個類股等權重時，共變異數項占變異數的 92.8%；只看變異數項，波動度只有 4.22%。波動度不能相加，所以 4.22% 不是 15.75% 的一部分。若平均變異數與平均共變異數都固定不變（思想實驗），類股越多，變異數項按 1/N 縮小，波動度趨近 15.45%，分散只能壓低變異數項；實際加入的類股會帶來自己的變異數與共變異數。若權重隨價格漂移（買進持有），報酬就不是同一個 w 的 Xw，等式也就不成立。

Knowledge Check 3

Two assets have daily variances σ^11​=4 and σ^22​=1 and covariance σ^12​=−1, in %². Compute sp2​ for w=(0.2,0.8)⊤ and for (0.5,0.5)⊤, and check the bound sp​≤w⊤s for both.

Answer

For (0.2,0.8) the variance is 0.04(4)+0.64(1)+2(0.16)(−1)=0.48, so sp​=0.69% against 0.2(2)+0.8(1)=1.2%. For (0.5,0.5) it is 0.25(4)+0.25(1)+2(0.25)(−1)=0.75, so sp​=0.87% against 1.5%. A negative covariance puts both far below the bound.

5Positive Semidefinite and Positive Definite Matrices

test a symmetric matrix for positive definiteness and semidefiniteness with leading principal minors, pivots and all principal minors

Every covariance matrix gives non-negative variances. Take C3​ of Example 3, the correlation matrix of S3: at (1,−1,0)⊤ its quadratic form equals 2−2(0.575)=0.85, and at (0,1,−1)⊤ it equals 2−2(0.596)=0.808. Positive values at a few vectors say nothing about the others. Which symmetric matrices give a non-negative value at every vector, and how can a test settle the question for C3​?

DefinitionPositive semidefinite and positive definite matrices

A symmetric N×N matrix M is positive semidefinite (PSD) if x⊤Mx≥0 for every x, and positive definite (PD) if x⊤Mx>0 for every x=0. It is indefinite if its quadratic form takes both signs.

TheoremThe sample covariance matrix is positive semidefinite

For every matrix of returns X, the matrix Σ^ is PSD. It is PD exactly when X~ has full column rank, rankX~=N.

Proof. By (10.5), w⊤Σ^w=∥X~w∥2/T≥0, with equality exactly when X~w=0. By LM9, some w=0 has X~w=0 exactly when rankX~<N. ■

The theorem answers the case's second question: the book's variance is a squared length divided by T, and no squared length is negative.

Checking every x is impossible, so practice uses determinants. A principal minor of M is the determinant of a square submatrix that keeps the same rows as columns. A leading principal minor keeps the first k rows and columns: detMk​.

TheoremTests for positive (semi)definiteness

Let M be a symmetric N×N matrix.

  1. If M is PSD, every diagonal entry is non-negative, because mii​=h(ei​); if M is PD, every one is positive.
  2. The matrix is PD if and only if its leading principal minors are all positive: detMk​>0 for k=1,…,N (Sylvester's criterion).
  3. The matrix is PD if and only if Gaussian elimination without row exchanges runs with positive pivots, dk​>0 for every k.
  4. The matrix is PSD if and only if every principal minor is non-negative (stated without proof; Horn and Johnson 2013, ch. 7).
  5. If M is PSD, so is K⊤MK for every matrix K with N rows. If M is PD and K is square and invertible, K⊤MK is PD.

Tests 2 and 3 are one test: elimination does not change the leading minors, and it makes each block Mk​ triangular, so detMk​=d1​⋯dk​ (LM9). The Deep Dive below proves them by completing squares, as (7.4) did for N=2. The pivots are also the squares of the diagonal entries of the Cholesky factor of LM12. A third test, through the eigenvalues of M, arrives in LM11, which also measures how close to singular Σ^ is. Test 5 follows from x⊤K⊤MKx=(Kx)⊤M(Kx).

Test 5 with K=diag(s)−1, applied to (10.3), gives a rule: C is PSD exactly when Σ^ is. Rescaling cannot create or remove a negative variance, provided every si​>0. Exhibit 6 compares the tests on C3​.

Example 6Three tests on one matrix

Test C3​ of Example 3, with its entries as printed, by leading principal minors and by pivots.

Solution

The leading minors are 1, then 1−0.5752=0.669375, then the full determinant. Expanding along the first row,

detC3​​=1+2(0.575)(0.403)(0.596)−0.5752−0.4032−0.5962=0.427966.​
All three are positive, so C3​ is PD. The pivots are the ratios 1, 0.669375/1=0.6694 and 0.427966/0.669375=0.6394. Elimination gives the same numbers: subtracting 0.575 times row 1 from row 2 leaves 1−0.5752 in position (2,2).

Example 7When leading minors mislead

(a) Test diag(0,−1). (b) Round the Semiconductor and FinancialInsurance block of AΣ^3​ to whole %², and add their 50/50 mix, rebalanced daily, as a third asset. The mix's covariances are averages of the two rows, and its variance is 41​(570)+21​(262)+41​(364), so

M=​570262416​262364313​416313364.5​​.
Test M.

Solution

(a) The leading minors are 0 and 0, both non-negative, yet h(e2​)=−1. The principal minor that keeps only row and column 2 is −1<0, and test 4 catches it.

(b) The 1×1 principal minors are 570, 364 and 364.5. The 2×2 ones are 570(364)−2622=138,836, 570(364.5)−4162=34,709 and 364(364.5)−3132=34,709. The determinant is exactly 0, because column 3 is half the sum of columns 1 and 2. All seven minors are non-negative, so M is PSD, but it is not PD: x=(0.5,0.5,−1)⊤, half in each sector and short the mix, gives x⊤Mx=0.

Deep DivePositive pivots make a matrix positive definiteoptional · click to expand

Let M be symmetric with m11​>0, and write y=(x2​,…,xN​)⊤. Completing the square in x1​ gives

x⊤Mxkij​​=m11​(x1​+j≥2∑​m11​m1j​​xj​)2+y⊤Ky,=mij​−m11​mi1​m1j​​(i,j≥2).​
Here K is the (N−1)×(N−1) matrix that the first step of elimination leaves, and its first diagonal entry is the second pivot. If K is PD and x=0, then either y=0 and the second term is positive, or y=0, which forces x1​=0 and makes the first term positive. So m11​>0 and K PD make M PD.

Conversely, if M is PD, then m11​=h(e1​)>0. Choosing x1​ to make the bracket zero shows y⊤Ky=h(x)>0 for every y=0, so K is PD. Repeating the step on K shows that M is PD exactly when every pivot is positive. Because detMk​=d1​⋯dk​, that happens exactly when every leading principal minor is positive (Strang 2016, §6.5). ■

導讀半正定與正定的檢驗

樣本共變異數矩陣（sample covariance matrix）一定是半正定（positive semidefinite），因為 w⊤Σ^w 是一個向量（vector）長度的平方除以 T，不可能小於 0；中心化（centring）後的報酬矩陣若行滿秩（full column rank），樣本共變異數矩陣就是正定（positive definite）。實務上用行列式（determinant）檢驗：所有首主子行列式（leading principal minor）都大於 0，或高斯消去法（Gaussian elimination）的每個樞軸元（pivot）都大於 0，就是正定。半正定則要檢查所有主子式（principal minor），只看左上角的那幾個，會被 diag(0,−1) 騙過。只要 K 可逆（invertible），把矩陣換成 K⊤MK 就不改變正定性與半正定性，所以相關矩陣（correlation matrix）和共變異數矩陣同時是或同時不是半正定。

Knowledge Check 4

A symmetric 2×2 matrix has m11​=2, m22​=4 and m12​=3. Is it PSD? Find a vector that shows the answer.

Answer

No. Its determinant is 8−9=−1<0, a negative principal minor. Completing the square as in (7.4) suggests x=(3,−2)⊤, and indeed h(x)=2(9)+2(3)(3)(−2)+4(4)=−2<0.

6When Σ^ Fails: Singularity and Pairwise Deletion

explain why a sample covariance matrix is positive semidefinite, when it is singular, and how pairwise deletion produces a matrix that is not

Centring costs one dimension. Every column of X~ sums to zero, 1⊤X~=0⊤, so the T rows of X~ are linearly dependent and rankX~≤T−1. The matrices Σ^ and X~ have the same null space: X~w=0 gives Σ^w=0, and Σ^w=0 gives ∥X~w∥2=Tw⊤Σ^w=0. By (9.7) of LM9 they have the same rank, so

rankΣ^=rankX~≤min(N,T−1).(10.7)

With T≤N returns, Σ^ is singular whatever the data.

Example 8Twenty-eight sectors, twenty-eight days

Compute Σ^ for U28 from the latest T returns, for T=20,…,35. When does it become PD?

Solution

By (10.7) the rank is at most T−1 while T≤28, and Exhibit 7 shows that it reaches that bound. On the latest 28 returns, from 28 August to 8 October 2026, the rank is 27, and Σ^ is singular. On the latest 29, from 27 August, it is 28: full rank, so Σ^ is PD.

Collinear returns also make Σ^ singular. Add to S5 a sixth column: the S5 equal-weight book, rebalanced daily. Its return is the average of the five columns on every date, so x=(51​,…,51​,−1)⊤ gives Xx=0, X~x=0 and x⊤Σ^x=0. The 6×6 matrix has rank 5. In floating point, x⊤Σ^x prints as a residue below 10−15 in absolute value, not as 0.

PitfallRounding and floating point

A matrix rounded entry by entry can stop being PSD. The covariance matrix of Semiconductor, FinancialInsurance and their 50/50 mix, computed from the data, is singular. Annualize it in %², like AΣ^3​, and round it to one decimal: its upper triangle reads 570.3, 261.8, 416.1; 363.7, 312.8; 364.4. Its determinant is then −13,888.91, a negative principal minor. Build a printed matrix from printed inputs, as Example 7 did.

In code, an exact zero appears as a tiny residue that differs between machines, so compare with a tolerance. Its size scales with the entries: below 10−15 for the daily 6×6 matrix above, larger for the 50/50 matrix in %². matrix_rank decides rank with a tolerance too, which LM12 explains.

Pairwise deletion

Series that start on different dates force a choice. Add 0050, 00631L and 00679B to U28. A common sample keeps only the dates on which all 31 series have returns: 2,357 returns from 18 January 2017, the day after 00679B's first close. Pairwise deletion computes each entry on the dates its own pair shares, Tij​ of them, here from 2,362 to 4,382. It keeps more data, but it mixes samples.

Write Σ^pw​ and Cpw​ for the covariance and correlation matrices that pairwise deletion builds. The ETF returns here are one-session total returns: from one trading date to the next, with both closes present and cash dividends added. The sector indices are price indices (Taiwan Stock Exchange 2023), so the matrices also mix return types.

Elimination on Σ^pw​ meets a negative pivot at step 29, the 0050 column (d29​=−3.66×10−6). Its leading 29×29 minor is therefore negative, so the matrix is not PSD (Exhibit 8), and some book gets a negative "variance". The unit vector with 0.656 in Semiconductor, −0.454 in 00631L, −0.362 in 0050 and smaller entries elsewhere gives x⊤Σ^pw​x=−6.56×10−6 a day. That is the negative variance of the case's third question. LM11 finds such a vector as the eigenvector of the smallest eigenvalue.

The cause is a mismatch between the diagonal and the rest. Each variance uses its series' whole sample, but each covariance with an ETF uses only the ETF's dates, on which Semiconductor was more volatile. So the correlation that Σ^pw​ implies between Semiconductor and 00631L is the pairwise one times 2.5076/2.3234​=1.039. Adding 0050 alone or 00631L alone to U28 already breaks the matrix; adding 00679B alone does not.

The common sample avoids the problem, but it has a cost. It drops the returns from 2 December 2008 to 17 January 2017, and 11 dates around the trading halts of 0050 (June 2025) and 00631L (March 2026). It also moves some sector correlations by as much as 0.144. ElectronicProductsDistribution and TradingConsumersGoods, for example, correlate at 0.465 on all dates but at 0.321 from 2017.

Example 9A risk system that prints a negative variance (constructed)

A risk system computes correlations pairwise, and some years are missing, by construction here. It keeps 0050's returns for 2018 and 2023, 00631L's for 2018 and 2019, and 00679B's for 2019 and 2023. So each pair shares one year, and no date has all three (Exhibit 9). Test the resulting Cpw​, and find a book with a negative "variance".

Solution

The pairs give ρ12​=0.982 (2018), ρ13​=0.199 (2023) and ρ23​=−0.444 (2019), where 1, 2 and 3 are 0050, 00631L and 00679B. Expanding the determinant,

detCpw​​=1+2(0.982)(0.199)(−0.444)−0.9822−0.1992−0.4442=−0.374592<0,​
so Cpw​ has a negative principal minor and is not PSD. The book x=(−1,1,1)⊤, in standard-deviation units, gives
​x⊤Cpw​x=3+2(−0.982−0.199−0.444)=−0.25.​
Shorting 0050 against 00631L cancels most of the risk (ρ12​=0.982), and 00679B is negatively correlated with 00631L. No sample has this matrix, so −0.25 is a number a risk system would print, not a variance. On the common dates of 2018 alone the three funds give 0.982, −0.394 and −0.395, and then detC=0.0301>0.

The years are not a rare choice. Of the 720 ways to give the three pairs three different calendar years from 2017 to 2026, 362 produce a negative determinant. Here 00679B's 2017 starts on 18 January, and 2026 runs to 8 October.

The widget below finds a book with a negative "variance" for any Cpw​ that is not PSD. It uses the adjugate, the transposed matrix of cofactors, with MadjM=(detM)I (LM9, Deep Dive). For a symmetric 3×3 matrix M, column j of the adjugate, x=adj(M)ej​, gives x⊤Mx=detM⋅adj(M)jj​. That value is negative when detM<0 and the 2×2 principal minor adj(M)jj​ is positive (Practice Problem 7).

Repairing a correlation matrix that is not PSD, for example with the nearest valid one (Rousseeuw and Molenberghs 1993; Higham 2002b), is left to LM30.

導讀共變異數矩陣什麼時候會壞掉

中心化（centring）之後每一行加總為 0，所以 T 筆報酬的秩（rank）最多是 T−1，28 個類股只用最近 28 天，共變異數矩陣（covariance matrix）必然是奇異矩陣（singular matrix）。某一行若是其他行的固定組合，例如每天再平衡的等權重組合，也會奇異。按配對刪除（pairwise deletion）讓每一格各自用兩個序列共同的日期，資料用得多，卻把不同樣本拼在一起，結果可能連半正定（positive semidefinite）都不是，風控系統就會對某個部位算出負的「變異數（variance）」。真實資料就發生了：類股加上 0050、00631L、00679B，按配對算出的共變異數矩陣，消去到第 29 步出現負的樞軸元（pivot）。

Knowledge Check 5

Why can Cpw​ be PD while Σ^pw​ is not, although (10.3) links a correlation matrix to a covariance matrix?

Answer

Formula (10.3) links a C and a Σ^ computed from the same sample. Pairwise, each correlation standardizes its pair with that pair's own standard deviations, while Σ^pw​ puts each series' whole-sample variance on its diagonal. The two matrices are built from different numbers, and neither is guaranteed to be PSD; here only Σ^pw​ failed.

7Matrix Calculus: Gradients, the Hessian and Convexity

derive the gradient and Hessian of a⊤w and w⊤Mw, and price a change of weights exactly with the expansion of a quadratic form
prove that a quadratic function is convex exactly when its matrix is positive semidefinite

LM7 differentiated the two-asset variance and found the Hessian H=2Σ. The same calculus works for N assets, one coordinate at a time. For a vector a, the partial derivative ∂(a⊤w)/∂wi​ is ai​. In w⊤Mw, the variable wi​ appears in row i and in column i of the double sum, so its partial derivative is ∑j​mij​wj​+∑j​mji​wj​. Stacked into vectors,

∇(a⊤w)=a,H=M+M⊤,∇(w⊤Mw)=(M+M⊤)w.​(10.8)

For symmetric M the gradient is 2Mw and the Hessian is 2M. For sp2​ they are 2Σ^w and 2Σ^: the Hessian H=2Σ of LM7, now for N assets.

The third derivatives of a quadratic function are zero, so the expansion (7.2) of LM7 ends at the second order with no remainder. For symmetric M, expanding the products gives

h(w+Δ)=h(w)+2Δ⊤Mw+Δ⊤MΔ.(10.9)

The middle term, 2Δ⊤Mw=Δ⊤∇h(w), is the gradient's linear prediction, and the last term corrects it exactly.

A fully invested book trades weight for weight, so 1⊤Δ=0. Adding the same number to every entry of the gradient ∇h(w) then leaves the linear term Δ⊤∇h(w) unchanged: only differences of entries matter. For the variance, a switch from asset j to asset i lowers sp2​ to first order when ∂sp2​/∂wi​<∂sp2​/∂wj​.

Example 10Switching weight from one sector to another

In the equal-weight U28 book, move 281​ of capital from GlassCeramic, the most volatile sector, to CommunicationsInternet, the least volatile. So Δ has 281​ in CommunicationsInternet, −281​ in GlassCeramic and 0 elsewhere. Use the annualized gradient 2AΣ^w and (10.9) to find the new variance and volatility.

Solution

The GlassCeramic entry of the gradient is 0.072303, the largest of the 28, and the CommunicationsInternet entry is 0.027641, the smallest. The linear term is

2AΔ⊤Σ^w​=280.027641−0.072303​=−0.0015951.​
The quadratic term, AΔ⊤Σ^Δ=+0.0001364, uses the two variances and their covariance. So the annualized variance of 0.0248034 becomes
​0.0248034−0.0015951+0.0001364=0.0233447,​
and the sample volatility would have fallen from 15.75% to 15.28%. The result is exact; the linear term alone would give 15.23%.

The gradient points in the direction of steepest ascent and is perpendicular to the level curve through its point (LM7). Exhibit 10 draws it for two sectors. The pitfall of Section 4 applies to it too: entry i of 2Σ^w is a rate of change, not asset i's share of the risk (LM27, LM31).

For symmetric M, any x, y and ω∈[0,1], expanding the products gives

h(ωx+(1−ω)y)​=ωh(x)+(1−ω)h(y)−ω(1−ω)h(x−y).​(10.10)
TheoremConvexity of a quadratic function

Let M be symmetric and h(x)=x⊤Mx. Then h is convex exactly when M is PSD, and strictly convex exactly when M is PD.

Proof. If M is PSD, the last term of (10.10) is not positive, so h(ωx+(1−ω)y)≤ωh(x)+(1−ω)h(y): the chord lies above the graph. If M is PD, x=y and 0<ω<1, the inequality is strict. The converse is in the Deep Dive. ■

Deep DiveA convex quadratic function has a PSD matrixoptional · click to expand

Let h be convex. For every x, the midpoint of x and −x is 0, so

0=h(0)≤21​h(x)+21​h(−x)=h(x),
and M is PSD. If h is strictly convex and x=0, the inequality is strict, and M is PD.

Portfolio variance w⊤Σ^w is therefore convex, with Hessian 2Σ^. For functions that are not quadratic, the same conclusion needs the argument of LM29. Finding the portfolio of least variance is the subject of LM28; this module stops at the gradient.

導讀矩陣微積分與凸性

對 w⊤Mw 逐一對 wi​ 求偏導數（partial derivative），wi​ 同時出現在第 i 列與第 i 行，所以梯度（gradient）是 (M+M⊤)w，矩陣對稱（symmetric）時就是 2Mw，海森矩陣（Hessian）是 2M。二次函數（quadratic function）的三階導數（third derivative）全為 0，泰勒展開（Taylor expansion）到二次就完全精確：把 1/28 的資金從玻璃陶瓷移到通信網路，樣本期間的波動度會從 15.75% 降到 15.28%，一點誤差都沒有。總權重不變的換股只看梯度分量的差。二次函數是凸函數（convex function）若且唯若矩陣半正定（positive semidefinite），這是 LM28 與 LM29 求解最佳化的基礎。

Knowledge Check 6

For the unsymmetric M of Example 1, compute ∇h at x=(1,1)⊤ by (10.8), and check it against 2Msym​x.

Answer

The matrix M+M⊤ has diagonal entries 2 and off-diagonal entries 4, so ∇h(1,1)=(6,6)⊤. Also 2Msym​x=2(1+2,2+1)⊤=(6,6)⊤, as it must be. Directly, h=x12​+4x1​x2​+x22​ has partial derivatives 2x1​+4x2​=6 and 4x1​+2x2​=6.

8Quadratic Forms and Covariance in Python

compute covariance matrices, portfolio variances and definiteness tests in NumPy and Polars with the right orientation, divisor and tolerance

The code below builds Σ^ and C from a matrix of returns, checks (10.4), and tests a matrix by its pivots.

Python
import numpy as np

# X: T x N array of daily returns, rows = dates (Part 1 of the lab)
T, N = X.shape
Xc = X - X.mean(axis=0)               # centred: every column sums to 0
S = Xc.T @ Xc / T                     # (10.2), N x N
assert np.allclose(S, np.cov(X, rowvar=False, ddof=0))
s = np.sqrt(np.diag(S))
C = S / np.outer(s, s)                # (10.3)

w = np.full(N, 1 / N)                 # equal weights, rebalanced daily
print(np.var(X @ w), w @ S @ w)       # (10.4): equal up to rounding

def pivots(M):
    """Pivots of elimination without row exchanges (test 3)."""
    M = np.array(M, dtype=float)
    out = []
    for k in range(len(M)):
        out.append(M[k, k])
        if M[k, k] <= 0:
            break                     # not PD: stop at this pivot
        M[k + 1:] -= np.outer(M[k + 1:, k] / M[k, k], M[k])
    return np.array(out)

print(pivots(C).min() > 0, np.linalg.matrix_rank(S))
# a pivot that is 0 in exact arithmetic can appear slightly negative:
# judge its sign with a tolerance (LM12)

# pairwise deletion with missing values (NaN): one mask per pair
ok = ~np.isnan(X)
both = ok[:, 0] & ok[:, 1]            # dates on which assets 1 and 2 trade
a, b = X[both, 0], X[both, 1]
cov_12 = np.mean((a - a.mean()) * (b - b.mean()))   # T_12 dates

Software differs in orientation, divisor and missing values, and Exhibit 11 lists the calls this module uses. Polars computes pl.cov and pl.corr on the rows where both columns have values, which is pairwise deletion without a warning.

In PythonCompanion lab

The Polars-first notebook LM10_lab.ipynb repairs the sector closes, builds Σ^ three ways and reproduces the exhibits and computational examples. It tests matrices for definiteness, rebuilds the pairwise-deletion case and solves the computational practice problems.

The notebook reads FinMind files that you download once with your own token. From the repository root, run uv run python data/fetch_finmind.py, then uv run python data/make_lab_data.py. FinMind's licence does not allow the book to redistribute the data. After that, the notebook runs offline.

Knowledge Check 7

A colleague runs np.cov(X) on a 4,382×28 array of returns. What are the shape and the largest possible rank of the result?

Answer

np.cov treats rows as variables, so the result is 4,382×4,382: covariances between dates, each computed across 28 sectors. Each "variable" has 28 observations, so by (10.7), with the roles of dates and assets swapped, its rank is at most 27.

Summary

  • A quadratic form x⊤Mx depends only on the symmetric part of M (10.1); definiteness is tested on Msym​.
  • The sample covariance matrix X~⊤X~/T (10.2) has 406 distinct entries for U28; (10.3) converts it to correlations and back.
  • A daily-rebalanced book's sample variance is exactly w⊤Σ^w (10.4). In the case, covariances made 92.8% of it by (10.6). The variance terms alone, 7.2% of it, would give a volatility of only 4.22%, against the book's 15.75%.
  • Every sample covariance matrix is PSD by (10.5), and PD exactly when the centred returns have full column rank.
  • Positive leading principal minors or pivots prove PD; PSD needs every principal minor, and rounding can destroy it.
  • The rank is at most min(N,T−1) (10.7). Pairwise deletion mixes samples, and with U28 and three ETFs it breaks PSD.
  • The gradient of w⊤Mw is (M+M⊤)w (10.8), the expansion (10.9) is exact, and a quadratic function is convex exactly when its matrix is PSD (10.10).

Solutions

  1. B is correct. Its leading minors are 2, 4−1=3 and 2(4−1)−1(2−0)=4, all positive. Matrix MA​ has leading minors 2, 3 and 2(4−9)−1(2)=−12<0, so it is not PD. Matrix MC​ has leading minors 1, 0 and 0, so it is not PD either. Its seven principal minors are 1, 1 and 1, then 0, 1 and 1, then 0; none is negative, so it is PSD by test 4. Indeed, its form is (x1​+x2​)2+x32​≥0, and MC​(1,−1,0)⊤=0, so it is singular.

  2. C is correct. Only Msym​ matters, with m11​=2, m22​=3 and off-diagonal entries 3. Its determinant is 6−9=−3<0, so the form takes both signs: h(1,0)=2 but h(1,−1)=2−6+3=−1. A reads the triangular M, whose determinant is 6.

  3. A is correct. By (10.7) the rank is at most min(28,20−1)=19, and Exhibit 7 shows that U28's latest 20 returns reach it. B forgets that centring removes one dimension, and C counts only the columns.

  4. By (10.3), entry (i,j) is the product of the two volatilities and the correlation. The diagonal is 23.882=570.25, 19.072=363.66 and 16.842=283.59. Off it, 23.88×19.07×0.575=261.85, 23.88×16.84×0.403=162.06 and 19.07×16.84×0.596=191.40, in %². For (0.2,0.3,0.5) the variance is

    ​0.04(570.25)+0.09(363.66)+0.25(283.59)+2(0.06(261.85)+0.1(162.06)+0.15(191.40))=247.69,​
    and the volatility is 247.69​=15.74%.

  5. By (10.6), with one fifth of var and 0.8 times cov, the daily variance is

    sp2​​=4.1480×10−5+7.2557×10−5=1.14037×10−4.​
    Annualized, 245.48×1.14037×10−4=0.027994, a volatility of 16.73%. The limit is 245.48×9.0696×10−5​=14.92%. Five sectors leave the book 1.81 points above its limit, and 28 sectors leave it 0.30 points above. The limit depends on the average covariance of the sectors chosen.

  6. The first pivot is d1​=570.34. Subtract 261.83/570.34 times row 1 from row 2, and 162.26/570.34 times row 1 from row 3. Rows and columns 2 and 3 then hold the block K of the Deep Dive in Section 5, with kij​=mij​−mi1​m1j​/570.34:

    K=(243.5299116.8602​116.8602237.3775​).
    For example, k22​=363.73−261.832/570.34. So d2​=243.5299, and one more step leaves
    d3​=237.3775−243.5299116.86022​=181.3010.
    The pivots 570.34, 243.53 and 181.30 are all positive, so the matrix is PD (test 3).

  7. Because MadjM=(detM)I, the vector x satisfies Mx=Madj(M)ej​=(detM)ej​. So x⊤Mx=(detM)x⊤ej​=(detM)xj​, and xj​=adj(M)jj​. That entry is the cofactor of mjj​: the 2×2 principal minor without row and column j. For the Cpw​ of Example 9 these minors are 1−0.4442=0.802864, 1−0.1992=0.960399 and 1−0.9822=0.035676, so the forms are −0.374592 times each: −0.3007, −0.3598 and −0.0134.

  8. By (10.8), the gradient is

    ∇u​=a−Mf=(0.10−0.045,0.04−0.02)⊤=(0.055,0.020)⊤.​
    By (10.9), applied to −21​M, the change is
    Δ⊤∇u−21​Δ⊤MΔ​=0.0035−21​(0.0004)=0.0033.​
    Directly, u moves from 0.0925 to 0.0958. Where ∇u=0 lie the Kelly exposures of LM43.

  9. In decimal units the printed matrix gives the gradient 2AΣ^3​w=(0.07923,0.05566,0.03905)⊤. With Δ=(−0.05,0,0.05)⊤ the linear term of (10.9) is

    0.05(0.03905−0.07923)=−0.002009,
    and the quadratic term is
    ​0.052(0.057034+0.028354−2×0.016226)=+0.000132.​
    So the variance moves from 0.032063 to
    ​0.032063−0.002009+0.000132=0.030186,​
    and the volatility falls from 17.91% to 17.37%. The printed matrix gives 320.63 %² for the starting mix, where the unrounded entries of Exhibit 5 give 320.62.

  10. If M is PSD, then h(x−y)≥0, and (10.10) gives h(ωx+(1−ω)y)≤ωh(x)+(1−ω)h(y) for every ω∈[0,1]. For Example 1, h(x)=x12​+4x1​x2​+x22​. Take x=(1,0)⊤, y=(0,1)⊤ and ω=21​. Then h(21​,21​)=1.5, but 21​h(x)+21​h(y)=1. The excess 0.5 is ω(1−ω) times −h(x−y)=2.

  11. The three matrices agree to within 10−15, and so do np.var(X @ w) and w @ S @ w, so (10.4) holds within floating-point rounding. The volatility of the equal-weight S5 book moves from 16.7313% to 16.7332% with ddof=1, the factor T/(T−1)​=1.000114 of Section 3.

Glossary

Term 中文 Meaning
Quadratic form 二次形式 x⊤Mx=∑i​∑j​mij​xi​xj​, (10.1).
Symmetric matrix 對稱矩陣 M=M⊤; every quadratic form has one, Msym​.
Sample covariance matrix 樣本共變異數矩陣 Σ^=X~⊤X~/T, (10.2).
Correlation matrix 相關矩陣 C=diag(s)−1Σ^diag(s)−1, (10.3).
Positive semidefinite (PSD) 半正定 x⊤Mx≥0 for every x.
Positive definite (PD) 正定 x⊤Mx>0 for every x=0.
Indefinite 不定 The quadratic form takes both signs.
Principal minor 主子式 Determinant of a submatrix with the same rows as columns.
Leading principal minor 首主子行列式 detMk​, from the first k rows and columns.
Pivot 樞軸元 Diagonal entry left by Gaussian elimination, dk​=detMk​/detMk−1​.
Singular matrix 奇異矩陣 A square matrix without full rank.
Pairwise deletion 按配對刪除 Each entry computed on the dates its own pair shares.
Adjugate 伴隨矩陣 Transposed matrix of cofactors; MadjM=(detM)I.
Gradient 梯度 ∇(w⊤Mw)=(M+M⊤)w, (10.8).
Hessian 海森矩陣 Matrix of second partial derivatives; 2M for a symmetric quadratic form.
Convex function 凸函數 Chords lie above the graph; for x⊤Mx, exactly when M is PSD.
